questions.question: Which of the following features are displayed by all cells under a microscope?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only plasma membrane and cytoplasm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **cell** is the fundamental **structural and functional unit** of all living organisms. While cells vary significantly in shape and size, they share core components visible under a **microscope**.
 
• The **plasma membrane** is the outermost selective boundary of the cell. It is present in **every living cell**, acting as a gatekeeper to regulate the movement of substances in and out of the cell. *Hence, this feature is displayed by all cells.*
 
• The **cytoplasm** is the semi-fluid, jelly-like matrix that fills the interior of the cell. It serves as the primary site for **metabolic reactions** and contains various **organelles** and molecular building blocks. *Hence, this feature is displayed by all cells.*
 
• The **nucleus** is a membrane-bound organelle containing **genetic material (DNA)**. However, it is only present in **eukaryotic cells**. **Prokaryotic cells** (such as **bacteria**) lack a defined **nuclear membrane**, and their genetic material is found in a region called the **nucleoid**.
 
• Because **prokaryotes** do not possess a true **nucleus**, it cannot be a feature displayed by **all** cells under a microscope. Therefore, only the **plasma membrane** and **cytoplasm** are universally present across all cell types. *Hence, the statement regarding only plasma membrane and cytoplasm is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prokaryotic Cells:**
 
 
• These cells are generally small, ranging from **1 to 10 µm**.
 
• They lack **membrane-bound organelles** like mitochondria, lysosomes, or Golgi bodies.
 
• Examples include **Bacteria**, **Archaea**, and **Cyanobacteria** (blue-green algae).
 
 
 
• **Eukaryotic Cells:**
 
 
• These cells are larger, typically **10 to 100 µm** in size.
 
• They possess a **well-defined nucleus** and complex membrane-bound organelles.
 
• Examples include **Plant cells**, **Animal cells**, **Fungi**, and **Protists**.
 
 
 
• **Plasma Membrane Composition:**
 
 
• It is primarily composed of **lipids** (mostly **phospholipids**) and **proteins**.
 
• It exhibits **selective permeability**, which is crucial for maintaining **homeostasis** within the cell.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Material:**
 
 
• While a **nucleus** is not universal, **DNA** or **genetic material** is a universal requirement for life, though its packaging varies between the **nucleoid** (prokaryotes) and **nucleus** (eukaryotes).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Cell Theory:** This theory was formulated by **M.J. Schleiden** and **Theodore Schwann** in the **1830s**. It states that all living things are composed of cells and that the cell is the basic unit of life.
 
• **Modern Cell Theory:** **Rudolf Virchow** expanded the theory in **1855** by stating "**Omnis cellula e cellula**," meaning all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
 
• **Microscopy:** To observe these features, biologists often use **staining agents**. For example, **Methylene Blue** is commonly used to stain animal cells to make the **nucleus** and **plasma membrane** more visible, while **Safranin** is used for plant tissues.
 
• **Exceptions:** **Viruses** are considered non-cellular or acellular entities because they do not have a **plasma membrane** or **cytoplasm** of their own, existing instead as **genetic material** encased in a **protein coat**.

questions.question: Which of the following help in maintaining the supply of nutrients to the growing plants in the forest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Decomposers** are microorganisms, such as **bacteria** and **fungi**, that play a vital role in the forest ecosystem by breaking down **dead organic matter**.
 
• They convert the **dead remains** of plants and animals into a dark, nutrient-rich substance known as **humus**.
 
• The **humus** created by these microorganisms ensures that essential **minerals** and **nutrients** are returned to the **soil**, making them available for uptake by the **roots** of growing plants.
 
• By recycling nutrients, **decomposers** maintain the continuous **nutrient cycle** in the forest, which is necessary for the sustained **growth** and **health** of the vegetation. ***Hence, the statement regarding decomposers is correct.***
 
• Without the action of decomposers, the forest floor would be covered in **waste**, and the soil would eventually lose the **fertility** required to support **producers**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Primary Consumers:**
 
 
• These are **herbivores** that feed directly on **producers** (green plants). Examples include **deer**, **rabbits**, and **grasshoppers**.
 
• Their main function is to transfer **energy** from plants to the higher levels of the **food chain**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Secondary Consumers:**
 
 
• These are **carnivores** or **omnivores** that feed on **primary consumers**. Examples include **frogs**, **small birds**, and **snakes**.
 
• They help regulate the **population** of herbivores within the **ecosystem**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Consumers:**
 
 
• These are **top predators** that feed on secondary consumers. Examples include **lions**, **tigers**, and **eagles**.
 
• They occupy the **highest trophic level** in a food chain and have fewer natural predators. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Producers:**
 
 
• These are **autotrophs**, mainly green plants, that manufacture their own food through the process of **photosynthesis** using **sunlight**, **water**, and **carbon dioxide**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Humus:** This is the **organic component** of soil, formed by the **decomposition** of leaves and other plant material by soil microorganisms. It improves soil **structure** and **moisture retention**.
 
• **Saprotrophs:** This is another term for **decomposers** that feed on dead and decaying matter by secreting **digestive enzymes** externally and absorbing the resulting **organic molecules**.
 
• **Nutrient Cycling:** This refers to the movement and exchange of **organic** and **inorganic matter** back into the production of living matter. It is a fundamental process that links **biotic** and **abiotic** components of the environment.
 
• **Biodiversity in Forests:** A healthy forest contains a wide variety of **decomposers**, which ensures that different types of **organic waste** (wood, leaves, bone, etc.) are processed efficiently at different **rates**.
</ul

questions.question: Which type of bond is present between carbon atoms in saturated hydrocarbons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Single bond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons** are organic compounds consisting entirely of **hydrogen** and **carbon** atoms where all the carbon-carbon bonds are **Single bonds**.
 
• These compounds are also widely known as **Alkanes** or **paraffins**. The term "saturated" implies that the carbon skeleton is bonded to the **maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms**.
 
• In these molecules, every **carbon atom** is **sp3 hybridized**, forming four sigma bonds in a **tetrahedral** geometry with bond angles of approximately **109.5 degrees**.
 
• The general chemical formula for acyclic (chain-like) saturated hydrocarbons is **CnH2n+2**, where **n** represents the **number of carbon atoms**. For example, if **n=1**, the compound is **Methane (CH4)**; if **n=2**, it is **Ethane (C2H6)**.
 
• Because **Single bonds** (sigma bonds) are relatively strong and stable, saturated hydrocarbons are generally **less reactive** compared to unsaturated hydrocarbons and do not undergo addition reactions under normal conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Unsaturated Hydrocarbons**:
 
 
• Unlike saturated hydrocarbons, **Unsaturated hydrocarbons** contain at least one **double bond** or **triple bond** between adjacent carbon atoms.
 
• **Alkenes**: These are unsaturated hydrocarbons containing at least one **carbon-carbon double bond** (C=C). Their general formula is **CnH2n**. A common example is **Ethene (C2H4)**.
 
• **Alkynes**: These contain at least one **carbon-carbon triple bond** (C≡C). Their general formula is **CnH2n-2**. The simplest alkyne is **Ethyne (C2H2)**, also known as **acetylene**.
 
 
 
• **Cycloalkanes**:
 
 
• These are **saturated hydrocarbons** where the carbon atoms are arranged in a **ring**. Although they only contain **Single bonds**, their general formula is **CnH2n** (same as alkenes) because the ring formation requires the loss of two hydrogen atoms.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reactivity**:
 
 
• Saturated hydrocarbons primarily undergo **substitution reactions** (such as halogenation under UV light) where a hydrogen atom is replaced by another atom or group.
 
• In contrast, unsaturated hydrocarbons are highly reactive and easily undergo **addition reactions** across the **double or triple bonds**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tetravalency of Carbon**: In all hydrocarbons, **Carbon** always maintains a valency of **4**, meaning it forms **four covalent bonds** to satisfy its octet.
 
• **Bond Strength**: The **Single bond** in alkanes is a **sigma (σ) bond**, which is formed by the head-on overlap of atomic orbitals. It is generally stronger and requires more energy to break than the **pi (π) bonds** found in double and triple bonds.
 
• **Physical State**: Smaller alkanes (**C1 to C4**) like methane and butane are **gases** at room temperature, while medium-sized ones (**C5 to C17**) are **liquids**, and larger ones are **solids** (like paraffin wax).
</ul

questions.question: What are the noticeable changes observed when an iron nail is placed in copper sulphate solution?

options.text: The iron nail becomes brownish in colour and the blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades.
The iron nail remains as it is and the blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades.
The iron nail becomes brownish in colour and the blue colour of the copper sulphate solution remains blue.
The iron nail becomes brownish in colour and the blue colour of the copper sulphate solution changes to yellow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The iron nail becomes brownish in colour and the blue colour of the copper sulphate solution fades**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an **iron nail (Fe)** is dipped in a **copper sulphate (CuSO4)** solution, a **displacement reaction** occurs because **iron** is more reactive than **copper**.
 
• During this process, **iron** displaces **copper** from the **copper sulphate** solution to form **iron sulphate (FeSO4)** and **solid copper**.
 
• The **blue colour** of the **copper sulphate** solution is due to the presence of **Cu2+ ions**. As the reaction progresses, these ions are replaced by **Fe2+ ions**, causing the **blue colour to fade** and eventually turn into a **light green colour**. *Hence, the statement regarding the fading of the blue colour is correct.*
 
• The **copper** metal that is displaced from the solution gets deposited on the surface of the **iron nail**. This result is seen as a **brownish coating** or layer on the nail. *Hence, the statement regarding the iron nail becoming brownish is correct.*
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: **Fe (s) + CuSO4 (aq) → FeSO4 (aq) + Cu (s)**. This illustrates the transition from **reactants** to **products** clearly.
 
• Therefore, the noticeable changes are the **fading of the blue colour** of the solution and the **brownish deposition** on the nail. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 1.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series:** 
 
 
• The **reactivity series** is a list of metals arranged in the order of their **decreasing activities**. Metals like **Potassium (K)** and **Sodium (Na)** are at the top, while **Gold (Au)** and **Platinum (Pt)** are at the bottom.
 
• In this series, **Iron (Fe)** is placed **above Copper (Cu)**, which explains why iron can displace copper from its salt solution, but copper cannot displace iron.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Reaction:** 
 
 
• A **displacement reaction** is a type of chemical reaction where a **more reactive element** displaces a **less reactive element** from its compound.
 
• This is a **single displacement reaction**. If two compounds exchange ions, it is called a **double displacement reaction**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Compounds:** 
 
 
• **Copper Sulphate (CuSO4):** Often found as **pentahydrate (CuSO4·5H2O)**, it is known as **Blue Vitriol** due to its vibrant **blue colour**.
 
• **Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4):** Often found as **heptahydrate (FeSO4·7H2O)**, it is known as **Green Vitriol**, which explains the **greenish tint** in the solution after the reaction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Redox Reaction:** 
 
 
• The reaction between the **iron nail** and **copper sulphate** is also an example of a **redox (reduction-oxidation) reaction**.
 
• **Iron** undergoes **oxidation** (loss of electrons): **Fe → Fe2+ + 2e-**.
 
• **Copper ions** undergo **reduction** (gain of electrons): **Cu2+ + 2e- → Cu**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Application:** 
 
 
• This experiment is a standard **laboratory demonstration** in **school chemistry** to teach the concept of **chemical changes** and **metal reactivity**.
 
• Before performing the experiment, the **iron nail** is usually cleaned with **sandpaper** to remove any **rust** or **grease**, ensuring the reaction occurs efficiently on the **metal surface**.
 
• The **time duration** for the reaction to show significant colour change is usually **15 to 30 minutes**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Read the given assertion (A) and reason (R) and select the most appropriate option.

(A): Oral contraceptive pills are a permanent method of contraception.
(R): They change hormone levels and prevent ovulation.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are false
A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A is false, but R is true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that oral contraceptive pills are a **permanent method** of contraception. This statement is **incorrect** because oral pills are categorized as **temporary or reversible methods** of birth control. ***Hence, statement A is false.***
 
• **Reason (R)** explains that these pills work by changing **hormone levels** and preventing **ovulation**. This is **correct** as the synthetic hormones in the pills suppress the secretion of **Follicle-Stimulating Hormone (FSH)** and **Luteinizing Hormone (LH)** from the pituitary gland. ***Hence, statement R is true.***
 
• Oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) are usually taken for a period of **21 days**, starting preferably within the first five days of the **menstrual cycle**. After a gap of **7 days** (during which menstruation occurs), the course is repeated.
 
• The primary mechanism involves the inhibition of **ovulation** and **implantation**, as well as altering the quality of **cervical mucus** to prevent or retard the entry of **sperms**.
 
• Because the effect of the medication wears off once the user stops taking the pills, fertility is restored, making it a **reversible method** rather than a permanent one.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Permanent Methods (Sterilization):**
 
 
• Unlike pills, **surgical methods** are considered **terminal or permanent** methods to prevent any more pregnancies.
 
• **Vasectomy**: This is the sterilization procedure for **males** where a small part of the **vas deferens** is removed or tied up through a small incision on the scrotum.
 
• **Tubectomy**: This is the sterilization procedure for **females** where a small part of the **fallopian tube** is removed or tied up through a small incision in the abdomen or through the vagina.
 
 
 
• **Types of Oral Pills:**
 
 
• **Combined Pills**: These contain both synthetic **estrogen** and **progesterone**. They are highly effective and are the most common type.
 
• **Saheli**: A unique oral contraceptive for females developed by the **Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI)** in **Lucknow**, India. It is a **non-steroidal** preparation taken **once a week** and has very few side effects.
 
• **Mini-pills**: These contain only **progestogen** and are often used by breastfeeding mothers or those who cannot take estrogen.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Contraceptive Efficacy**: Oral pills are very popular among **urban women** and have a very high **efficacy rate** when taken correctly, though they do not provide protection against **Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs)** or **AIDS**.
 
• **Hormonal Action**: The high levels of **progesterone** in the blood send a **negative feedback** signal to the hypothalamus and pituitary gland, preventing the mid-cycle surge of **LH**, which is essential for **ovulation**.
 
• **Implantation Interference**: Even if ovulation were to occur, the hormones in the pill alter the **endometrium** (lining of the uterus), making it unsuitable for the **implantation** of a fertilized egg.
 
• **Cervical Mucus**: The pills cause the **cervical mucus** to become thick and sticky, creating a physical barrier that is difficult for **sperm** to penetrate.
</ul

questions.question: Which statement is INCORRECT regarding mass and weight?

options.text: Mass is the measure of inertia, weight is the force due to gravity.
Mass has SI unit kg, weight has SI unit newton.
Mass is scalar, weight is vector.
Mass varies from place to place, weight remains constant.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass varies from place to place, weight remains constant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is a fundamental measure of the **amount of matter** in an object and serves as a measure of its **inertia**. **Inertia** is the resistance of any physical object to any change in its velocity. Weight, on the other hand, is the **force** exerted on an object due to **gravity**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **SI unit** of **mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**, which is one of the seven base units in the International System of Units. Since **weight** is a force (calculated as **W = mg**), its **SI unit** is the **newton (N)**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Mass** is a **scalar quantity** because it only has **magnitude** and no specific direction. **Weight** is a **vector quantity** because it has both magnitude and a **direction**, which is always directed toward the **center of the Earth** or the source of gravity. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Mass** is an **intrinsic property** of an object and remains **constant** regardless of its **location** in the universe. However, **weight varies** from place to place because it depends on the local **acceleration due to gravity (g)**. For instance, an object's weight on the **Moon** is about **1/6th** of its weight on **Earth**, while its mass remains identical. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Mass varies from place to place, weight remains constant (as it is the incorrect statement).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Measurement Tools**: 
 
 
• The **mass** of an object is typically measured using a **physical balance** or a **beam balance**, which compares an unknown mass with a known mass.
 
• The **weight** of an object is measured using a **spring balance**, which measures the **gravitational pull** stretching a spring.
 
 
 
• **Variation of 'g' on Earth**: 
 
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is not uniform everywhere on **Earth**. It is **maximum at the poles** (approx **9.83 m/s²**) and **minimum at the equator** (approx **9.78 m/s²**) due to the Earth's **ellipsoidal shape** and rotation.
 
• As a result, a person will **weigh slightly more at the North Pole** than at the **equator**, even though their **mass** remains exactly the same.
 
 
 
• **Zero Weight Condition**:
 
 
• While **mass can never be zero** for any physical matter, **weight can be zero**. This occurs in **interstellar space** far from any celestial body or during **free fall** (weightlessness), where the **effective gravity** becomes zero.
 
• At the **center of the Earth**, the **acceleration due to gravity** is **zero**, making the **weight** of any object **zero** at that specific **location**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mathematical Relationship**: The relationship between **weight (W)** and **mass (m)** is defined by **Newton’s Second Law** as **W = m × g**, where **g** is the local **gravitational acceleration**.
 
• **Inertial Mass vs. Gravitational Mass**: In classical physics, **inertial mass** (resistance to acceleration) and **gravitational mass** (response to gravity) are considered **equivalent**, a principle that forms the basis of **Einstein's General Theory of Relativity**.
 
• **Common Misconception**: In daily life, people often use **kilograms** to express **weight**. However, in **scientific terms**, **kilogram** is strictly a unit of **mass**, and **weight** should be expressed in **newtons**.

6f

questions.question: According to Newton’s third law, action and reaction forces:

options.text: cancel each other out because they are equal
act on the same object at the same time
act on the same object at different times
act on two different objects at the same time

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**act on two different objects at the same time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Third Law of Motion** states that for every **action**, there is an **equal** and **opposite reaction**.
 
• These forces always occur in **pairs**. If object **A** exerts a force on object **B**, then object **B** simultaneously exerts a force of **equal magnitude** and **opposite direction** on object **A**.
 
• Crucially, the action and reaction forces **act on two different objects**. Because they act on different bodies, they **cannot cancel each other out**, as cancellation of forces only occurs when multiple forces act on the **same** single body. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• The forces act **simultaneously**, meaning they happen at the **exact same time**. There is no cause-and-effect time lag between the action and the reaction. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Since the law specifically involves an interaction **between two bodies**, the forces cannot act on the same object. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Even though the forces are **equal in magnitude**, they do not **cancel each other** because they are applied to different entities. For a net force to be **zero** through cancellation, the opposing forces must be applied to the **same object**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law**: Also known as the **Law of Inertia**, it states that an object will remain at **rest** or in **uniform motion** in a straight line unless acted upon by an **external unbalanced force**.
 
• **Newton's Second Law**: This law defines force quantitatively, stating that the **acceleration** of an object is directly proportional to the **net force** acting on it and inversely proportional to its **mass**. The mathematical formula is **F = ma**.
 
• **The SI Unit of Force**: The standard unit of force is the **Newton** (represented by the symbol **N**), named after **Sir Isaac Newton** who published these laws in **1687** in his work **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica**.
 
• **Conservation of Momentum**: Newton's Third Law is the fundamental basis for the **Law of Conservation of Momentum**. In an isolated system where no **external forces** act, the total **momentum** remains **constant** over time.
 
• **Practical Examples**: 
 
 
• **Walking**: A person pushes the **ground backward** (action), and the ground pushes the **person forward** (reaction).
 
• **Recoil of a Gun**: When a **bullet** is fired (action), the **gun** jumps backward (reaction).
 
• **Rocket Propulsion**: The rocket pushes **exhaust gases** downward at high velocity, and the gases exert an **upward thrust** on the rocket.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Magnitude and Direction**: The magnitude of the action force is exactly **equal** to the magnitude of the reaction force, but their **directions** are exactly **180 degrees** apart (opposite).
 
• **Nature of Force**: The action and reaction forces are always of the **same nature**. If the action is a **magnetic force**, the reaction must also be a magnetic force; if the action is **friction**, the reaction is also friction.
 
• **Mass and Acceleration**: While the **forces** are equal, the resulting **accelerations** are usually not equal because the two objects typically have different **masses**. For instance, the **Earth** pulls a falling **apple** with the same force the apple pulls the Earth, but the Earth's acceleration is **negligible** due to its massive **mass**.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is least reactive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical reactivity of metals is determined by their ability to lose electrons and form positive ions. The **Reactivity Series** (or **Activity Series**) is an arrangement of metals in **descending order** of their reactivity.
 
• **Gold (Au)** is located at the **very bottom** of the reactivity series. This indicates that it is a **noble metal** with extremely low chemical reactivity, as it does not easily lose electrons to form compounds. ***Hence, the correct answer is Gold.***
 
• **Sodium (Na)** is an **alkali metal** placed near the top of the reactivity series. It is **highly reactive** and reacts vigorously with both water and oxygen at room temperature. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)** and **Zinc (Zn)** are placed in the middle of the series. While they are less reactive than **Sodium**, they are significantly more reactive than **Gold** and can react with acids and steam. ***Hence, options 1 and 3 are incorrect.***
 
• Because of its **inert nature**, **Gold** is found in its **native state** in nature and does not corrode or tarnish when exposed to air or water, even when heated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Reactivity Series Order:** The general order from most reactive to least reactive is: **Potassium (K)** > **Sodium (Na)** > **Calcium (Ca)** > **Magnesium (Mg)** > **Aluminium (Al)** > **Zinc (Zn)** > **Iron (Fe)** > **Lead (Pb)** > **[Hydrogen]** > **Copper (Cu)** > **Mercury (Hg)** > **Silver (Ag)** > **Gold (Au)**.
 
• **Sodium (Atomic Number 11):** It belongs to **Group 1** of the periodic table. Due to its extreme reactivity with atmospheric moisture and oxygen, it must be stored under **kerosene oil** to prevent accidental combustion.
 
• **Magnesium and Zinc:** **Magnesium (Atomic Number 12)** reacts with hot water and burns with a **dazzling white flame**. **Zinc (Atomic Number 30)** is widely used in the process of **galvanization** to protect iron from rusting, as it is more reactive than iron but forms a stable protective oxide layer.
 
• **Noble Metals and Aqua Regia:** Metals like **Gold** and **Platinum** are called **Noble Metals** because they are resistant to most acids. However, **Gold** can be dissolved in **Aqua Regia**, which is a freshly prepared mixture of **concentrated Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **concentrated Nitric acid (HNO3)** in a **ratio of 3:1**.
 
• **Displacement Reactions:** The reactivity series helps predict the outcome of displacement reactions, where a **more reactive metal** can displace a **less reactive metal** from its salt solution. For example, **Zinc** can displace **Copper** from **Copper Sulphate**, but **Gold** cannot displace any metal listed above it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gold's Physical Properties:** Besides its low reactivity, **Gold** is the most **malleable** and **ductile** metal known. It has a high **atomic number of 79** and is valued in **jewelry** and **electronics** due to its high electrical conductivity and resistance to **oxidation**.
 
• **Atomic Stability:** The low reactivity of **Gold** is partly due to the **relativistic effects** on its electrons, which make the **6s orbital** electrons more tightly bound to the nucleus, thus resisting chemical bonding.
</ul

questions.question: We express the concentration of solution in various ways. Which of the following method is INCORRECT?

options.text: Volume by volume percentage of a solution
Mass by mass percentage of a solution
Volume by mass percentage of a solution
Mass by volume percentage of a solution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Volume by mass percentage of a solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **concentration of a solution** is the amount of **solute** present in a given amount (**mass or volume**) of solution, or the amount of solute dissolved in a given mass or volume of **solvent**.
 
• **Mass by mass percentage** of a solution is calculated as the (**Mass of solute** / **Mass of solution**) × **100**. This is a common and correct method for expressing concentration, especially when dealing with two solid components. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Mass by volume percentage** of a solution is calculated as the (**Mass of solute** / **Volume of solution**) × **100**. This method is widely used in **medicine** and **pharmacy**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• **Volume by volume percentage** of a solution is calculated as the (**Volume of solute** / **Volume of solution**) × **100**. This is used when both the solute and the solvent are **liquids**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Volume by mass percentage** is not a standard or scientifically recognized method for expressing the concentration of a solution in general chemistry, as **volume** changes with **temperature** while **mass** remains constant, making this ratio inconsistent. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solute and Solvent**: In a **homogeneous mixture**, the component present in a **smaller quantity** is the **solute**, while the component present in the **larger quantity** is the **solvent**.
 
• **Molarity (M)**: It is defined as the number of **moles** of solute dissolved in **one litre** of solution. It is one of the most commonly used units of concentration in **laboratories**.
 
• **Molality (m)**: This is the number of **moles** of solute per **kilogram** (**kg**) of the **solvent**. Unlike molarity, molality does not change with **temperature**.
 
• **Saturated Solution**: A solution in which **no more solute** can be dissolved at a particular **temperature** is called a **saturated solution**. The amount of solute present in it at this temperature is called its **solubility**.
 
• **Parts Per Million (ppm)**: When a solute is present in **trace quantities**, the concentration is expressed in **ppm**. It is calculated as (**Number of parts of the component** / **Total number of parts of all components of the solution**) × **10⁶**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Temperature Dependence**: Concentration terms like **Molarity**, **Volume percentage**, and **Mass by Volume percentage** change with **temperature** because **volume** is dependent on temperature.
 
• **Temperature Independence**: Concentration terms like **Mass percentage**, **Molality**, and **Mole fraction** are **independent** of temperature because they are based on **mass**.
 
• **Mole Fraction**: It is the **ratio** of the number of moles of a particular component to the **total number of moles** of all the components in the solution. The sum of all mole fractions in a solution is always **equal to one**.

questions.question: What is the name of the fluid present inside a plant cell vacuole?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cell sap**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cell sap** is a **watery fluid** found specifically inside the **large central vacuole** of **plant cells**. It acts as a storage reservoir for various substances required by the plant. ***Hence, the correct option is Cell sap.***
 
• **Nucleoplasm** is the specialized **protoplasm** located within the **nuclear envelope** of a cell. It serves as a suspension medium for the **nucleolus** and **chromatin**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Protoplasm** is a broad term that refers to the **entire living content** of a cell, which includes both the **cytoplasm** and the **nucleus**. It is often described as the physical basis of life. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Cytoplasm** is the jelly-like substance that fills the cell and surrounds the organelles, located between the **cell membrane** and the **nuclear membrane**. While it contains many enzymes and nutrients, it is distinct from the fluid inside the vacuole. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **cell sap** plays a crucial role in maintaining **turgor pressure**, which provides **mechanical support** and **rigidity** to the plant structure, preventing it from wilting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Cell Sap**:
 
 
• It consists of **water**, **sugars** (like **sucrose**), **amino acids**, **mineral salts**, **organic acids**, and sometimes **pigments**.
 
• It also contains **metabolic waste products** that are sequestered away from the rest of the **cytoplasm** to prevent interference with cellular functions.
 
• The presence of **anthocyanin pigments** in the cell sap is responsible for the **red**, **purple**, or **blue** colors of many **flowers** and **fruits**.
 
 
 
• **The Tonoplast**:
 
 
• The **vacuole** is enclosed by a single unit membrane called the **tonoplast**.
 
• The **tonoplast** is a **semi-permeable membrane** that facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against **concentration gradients** into the vacuole, making their concentration significantly higher in the **cell sap** than in the **cytoplasm**.
 
 
 
• **Vacuole Characteristics**:
 
 
• In **mature plant cells**, the central vacuole can occupy up to **90%** of the **volume of the cell**.
 
• In contrast, **animal cells** have much **smaller**, **temporary vacuoles** that are used for **exocytosis** or **endocytosis**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Osmoregulation**: The **high concentration** of solutes in the **cell sap** allows the plant cell to absorb **water** from its surroundings through **osmosis**. This process is vital for **nutrient transport** and maintaining the plant's **water balance**.
 
• **Storage Function**: The **vacuole** acts as a "trash can" or "storage locker," keeping **toxic secondary metabolites** (like **alkaloids** or **tannins**) separate from the **cytosol** to protect the cell's **metabolic machinery**.
 
• **Historical Context**: The term **Protoplasm** was coined by **J.E. Purkinje** in **1839** to describe the living matter of the cell, while the **vacuole** was first discovered by **Antonie van Leeuwenhoek** in **1676**, though its function was understood much later.
</ul

questions.question: Which statement best supports the Law of Constant Proportions?

options.text: Mud from two ponds containing different minerals
Soil from two areas with mixed organic content
Water from two sources with identical composition
Sand from two places with varying grain size

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water from two sources with identical composition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Law of Constant Proportions**, also known as the **Law of Definite Proportions**, states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in a **fixed ratio by mass** and does not depend on its source or method of preparation.
 
• This fundamental law of chemistry was proposed by the **French chemist Joseph Proust** in the year **1799**.
 
• **Water (H2O)** is a classic example of a pure chemical compound. Regardless of whether it is sourced from a river, an ocean, or synthesized in a laboratory, it always contains **Hydrogen** and **Oxygen** in a mass ratio of approximately **1:8**. ***Hence, the statement regarding water from two sources with identical composition is correct.***
 
• Mud from two ponds containing different minerals refers to a **heterogeneous mixture**. Mixtures do not have a fixed chemical composition, and their properties vary based on the proportion of their constituents. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• Soil with mixed organic content is another example of a **mixture** where the components are not chemically bonded in a fixed ratio. The ratio of organic matter to minerals changes based on the **location** and **environment**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• Sand with varying grain sizes represents a **physical mixture** of particles. The "composition" in terms of grain size is a physical characteristic, not a chemical proportion of elements within a compound. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Laws of Chemical Combination:** These laws provide the mathematical and conceptual framework for **stoichiometry** and the study of chemical reactions.
 
 
• **Law of Conservation of Mass:** Formulated by **Antoine Lavoisier** in **1789**, it states that mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
 
• **Law of Multiple Proportions:** Proposed by **John Dalton** in **1803**, it states that if two elements form more than one compound, the ratios of the masses of the second element that combine with a fixed mass of the first element will be **small whole numbers**.
 
 
 
• **Distinction between Compounds and Mixtures:**
 
 
• **Compounds:** Substances formed by the **chemical union** of two or more elements in a **definite proportion by mass**. Examples include **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**, **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, and **Methane (CH4)**.
 
• **Mixtures:** Substances formed by physically mixing two or more substances without any **chemical bond**. Their composition can vary widely (e.g., air, alloys, or salt water).
 
 
 
• **Verification of the Law:** **Joseph Proust** performed extensive experiments on **cupric carbonate**. He compared samples of natural origin with synthetic samples prepared in the lab and found that the **percentage by weight** of **Copper**, **Carbon**, and **Oxygen** was identical in both.
 
• **Modern Perspective:** While the law is universally applicable to most compounds, some exceptions exist in the form of **non-stoichiometric compounds** (often metallic oxides or sulfides) and compounds containing different **isotopes** of the same element, which may slightly alter the mass ratio.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In **Water (H2O)**, the molar mass of **Hydrogen** is approximately **1 g/mol** and **Oxygen** is **16 g/mol**. Since there are two hydrogen atoms, the ratio is **2:16**, which simplifies to **1:8**.
 
• The Law of Constant Proportions was a key piece of evidence used by **John Dalton** to develop his **Atomic Theory** in the early **19th century**.
 
• Understanding these proportions is essential for **chemical engineering**, **pharmaceuticals**, and **analytical chemistry** to ensure the purity and consistency of products.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following quantities is a measure of the inertia of a body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inertia** is the inherent property of a physical body to resist any change in its state of **rest** or **uniform motion** in a straight line.
 
• The **Mass** of an object is a direct quantitative measure of its **inertia**. A body with a larger **mass** has a greater tendency to resist changes in its motion compared to a body with a smaller **mass**. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• According to **Newton's First Law of Motion**, often referred to as the **Law of Inertia**, an object will remain at rest or continue to move at a constant velocity unless acted upon by a net **external force**.
 
• The **SI unit** of mass is the **kilogram (kg)**. It is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has only magnitude and no direction.
 
• In classical mechanics, **mass** is considered constant for a body and does not change regardless of the body's **location** in the universe, unlike weight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Weight**:
 
 
• It is the **gravitational force** exerted on an object by a celestial body (like Earth).
 
• It is calculated using the formula **W = mg**, where **m** is mass and **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity** (approximately **9.8 m/s²** on Earth).
 
• Unlike **mass**, **weight** is a **vector quantity** and changes depending on the **location** (e.g., your weight on the **Moon** is about **1/6th** of your weight on **Earth**).
 
 
 
• **Force**:
 
 
• A **force** is a push or pull upon an object resulting from the object's interaction with another object.
 
• It is defined by **Newton's Second Law of Motion** as the product of mass and acceleration (**F = ma**).
 
• The **SI unit** of force is the **Newton (N)**.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration**:
 
 
• It is defined as the rate of change of **velocity** of an object with respect to **time**.
 
• It is a **vector quantity** measured in **meters per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Inertia**:
 
 
• **Inertia of Rest**: The inability of a body to change by itself its state of rest. For example, when a **bus** suddenly starts, passengers fall **backward**.
 
• **Inertia of Motion**: The inability of a body to change by itself its state of uniform motion. For example, when a moving **bus** stops suddenly, passengers jerk **forward**.
 
• **Inertia of Direction**: The inability of a body to change by itself its direction of motion. For example, when a **car** takes a sharp turn, passengers are thrown **outwards**.
 
 
 
• **Relationship between Mass and Inertia**:
 
 
• If you compare a **tennis ball** and a **cricket ball**, the cricket ball has more **mass**; therefore, it requires more **force** to change its state of motion, demonstrating higher **inertia**.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a nerve type with its origin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cranial nerves – Brain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cranial nerves** are a set of **12 pairs** of nerves that emerge directly from the **brain** and the **brainstem**. They primarily serve the sensory and motor functions of the head and neck region. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Cranial nerves** do not originate from the **spinal cord**; instead, they pass through various foramina (openings) in the **skull** to reach their target organs. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Spinal nerves** originate from the **spinal cord** and are part of the **Peripheral Nervous System (PNS)**. They are not produced by or originated from the **heart**, although some branches of the **autonomic nervous system** (like the **vagus nerve**, which is cranial) regulate cardiac functions. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Spinal nerves** specifically emerge from segments of the **spinal cord** through the **intervertebral foramina**. They do not originate from the **brain**, which is the origin point for cranial nerves. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• The human body contains **31 pairs** of **spinal nerves**, which are named according to the region of the **vertebral column** from which they emerge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cranial Nerves:**
 
 
• There are **12 pairs** of cranial nerves, designated by **Roman numerals (I-XII)**.
 
• Examples include the **Olfactory nerve (I)** for smell, the **Optic nerve (II)** for vision, and the **Vagus nerve (X)**, which has the most extensive distribution, reaching the **thorax** and **abdomen**.
 
• Most cranial nerves are **mixed nerves** (containing both sensory and motor fibers), though some like the **Olfactory** and **Optic** nerves are purely **sensory**.
 
 
 
• **Spinal Nerves:**
 
 
• There are **31 pairs** of spinal nerves in humans: **8 cervical**, **12 thoracic**, **5 lumbar**, **5 sacral**, and **1 coccygeal**.
 
• Every spinal nerve is a **mixed nerve**, carrying both **sensory** information toward the spinal cord and **motor** commands away from it.
 
• They form **plexuses** (networks), such as the **brachial plexus** which supplies the **arms** and the **lumbar plexus** which supplies the **legs**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nerve Classification by Function:**
 
 
• **Sensory (Afferent) Nerves:** Carry impulses from **receptors** (like skin or eyes) to the **Central Nervous System (CNS)**.
 
• **Motor (Efferent) Nerves:** Carry impulses from the **CNS** to **effectors** like **muscles** and **glands**.
 
 
 
• **Central vs. Peripheral Nervous System:**
 
 
• The **CNS** consists of the **brain** and the **spinal cord**.
 
• The **PNS** consists of all the nerves that branch out from the CNS to the rest of the body, including **cranial** and **spinal nerves**.
 
• The **Somatic Nervous System** controls **voluntary** movements, while the **Autonomic Nervous System** controls **involuntary** actions like **heart rate** and **digestion**.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a person with hypermetropia?

options.text: They are unable to see anything without glasses
Their vision is equally blurred for both near and distant objects
They can see nearby objects clearly but distant ones appear blurry
They can see faraway objects clearly but struggle to see things up close

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They can see faraway objects clearly but struggle to see things up close**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hypermetropia**, also commonly known as **farsightedness**, is a vision condition where a person can see distant objects clearly, but objects nearby appear blurry. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 4.***
 
• In a hypermetropic eye, the light rays coming from a nearby object are not focused on the **retina** but instead converge at a point **behind the retina**. This results in a blurred image for close-up tasks like reading or sewing.
 
• This defect arises because either the **focal length** of the eye lens is too long or the **eyeball** has become too **short**. Because the eye cannot increase its converging power sufficiently, the **near point** of the person moves farther away than the standard **25 cm**.
 
• To correct this vision defect, a **convex lens** (converging lens) of appropriate power is used. The lens provides the additional focusing power required to bring the light rays together exactly on the **retina**.
 
• A person with **hypermetropia** often experiences **eye strain** or headaches after performing close-work activities for a long duration due to the constant effort of the **ciliary muscles** to focus.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Myopia (Nearsightedness):**
 
 
• This is the opposite of hypermetropia, where a person can see nearby objects clearly but distant objects appear blurry.
 
• The image is formed **in front of the retina** rather than on it, often due to an **elongated eyeball** or excessive curvature of the lens.
 
• It is corrected using a **concave lens** (diverging lens), which diverges the light rays before they enter the eye, allowing them to focus correctly on the **retina**.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia:**
 
 
• This condition is associated with **aging**, usually occurring after the age of **40**. It is caused by the gradual weakening of the **ciliary muscles** and the diminishing flexibility of the **crystalline lens**.
 
• The person finds it difficult to see nearby objects comfortably without corrective glasses, similar to hypermetropia, but the underlying cause is **loss of accommodation**.
 
• It is often corrected using **bifocal lenses**, where the upper portion is concave for distant vision and the lower portion is convex for reading.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism:**
 
 
• This occurs when the **cornea** or the lens is not perfectly spherical, having different curvatures in different planes.
 
• As a result, light rays do not focus on a single point on the **retina**, causing vision to be blurred or distorted at all distances. It is typically corrected using **cylindrical lenses**.
 
 
 
• **Cataract:**
 
 
• This is a medical condition where the lens of the eye becomes **cloudy** or opaque, leading to a progressive loss of vision.
 
• It is most common in **older adults** and is treated through a surgical procedure where the cloudy lens is replaced with an artificial **intraocular lens (IOL)**.
 
 
 
• **Optical Power:**
 
 
• The power of a corrective lens is measured in **Dioptres (D)**. For **Hypermetropia**, the prescription power is **positive (+)**, whereas for **Myopia**, it is **negative (-)**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following occurs due to continuous movement of gas particles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diffusion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diffusion** is defined as the intermixing of particles of two different types of matter on their own. This process occurs due to the **continuous, random movement** of particles.
 
• In the context of **gases**, particles possess high **kinetic energy** and move at very high speeds in all directions. Because there are large **intermolecular spaces** between gas particles, they can easily move into the spaces of other substances.
 
• The **Kinetic Molecular Theory** of matter states that particles of matter are never at rest; they are in constant motion. This motion is most pronounced in **gases** compared to solids and liquids.
 
• The rate of **diffusion** increases with an increase in **temperature** because higher temperatures give particles more **kinetic energy**, making them move faster. ***Hence, statement 3 is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Condensation:**
 
 
• This is the process by which a substance changes from a **gaseous state** to a **liquid state**.
 
• It occurs when a gas is cooled or subjected to increased **pressure**, causing particles to lose energy and come closer together.
 
 
 
• **Melting:**
 
 
• Also known as **fusion**, it is the physical process where a **solid** turns into a **liquid**.
 
• This happens at a specific temperature called the **melting point**, where the heat energy overcomes the **intermolecular forces** holding the solid structure together.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation:**
 
 
• It is a **surface phenomenon** in which a liquid changes into **vapour** at any temperature below its boiling point.
 
• Unlike **diffusion**, which is the movement and mixing of particles, **evaporation** specifically refers to the phase transition from liquid to gas at the surface.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Brownian Motion:** This is the **zig-zag**, random motion of microscopic particles suspended in a fluid (liquid or gas) resulting from their collision with the fast-moving atoms or molecules in the gas or liquid. It was first observed by **Robert Brown** in **1827**.
 
• **Graham's Law of Diffusion:** Formulated by **Thomas Graham** in **1833**, this law states that the rate of **diffusion** or effusion of a gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its **molar mass**.
 
• **Applications:** Diffusion is responsible for many everyday occurrences, such as the **aroma of food** reaching us from several meters away, the spreading of **fragrance** from a perfume bottle, and the exchange of **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide** in the lungs.
</ul

questions.question: Megaphones, loudhailers, and shehnais are designed to:

options.text: convert sound waves into electrical signals
spread sound waves equally in all directions
focus sound waves in a particular direction
reduce the intensity of sound waves

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**focus sound waves in a particular direction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Megaphones**, **loudhailers**, and musical instruments like **shehnais** are specifically designed to send sound waves in a **particular direction** rather than allowing them to spread equally in all directions.
 
• These devices function based on the principle of **multiple reflection of sound**. They typically feature a **tube** followed by a **conical opening**.
 
• The **conical shape** acts as a reflective surface that directs the sound waves emitted from the source toward the front. As the sound waves hit the inner walls of the cone, they undergo **successive reflections**, which guides the sound energy forward toward the audience.
 
• By preventing the sound from dispersing into the surrounding environment, the **intensity** and **loudness** of the sound are significantly increased in the desired path. *Hence, the statement that they focus sound waves in a particular direction is correct.*
 
• The primary objective of this design is to ensure that the sound reaches a **longer distance** with clarity, making it ideal for public addresses or musical performances in open spaces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shehnai:**
 
 
• The **Shehnai** is a classical musical instrument (a **double-reed oboe**) prevalent in **India**, **Pakistan**, and **Bangladesh**.
 
• It was traditionally played in **royal courts** (as part of the **naubat**) and is now a staple in **North Indian weddings** and **temple ceremonies**.
 
• Legendary musician **Ustad Bismillah Khan** is credited with popularizing the **Shehnai** on the global classical stage and was awarded the **Bharat Ratna** in **2001**.
 
 
 
• **Reflection of Sound:**
 
 
• Like light, sound reflects off **solid** or **liquid** surfaces. It follows the **laws of reflection**, where the **angle of incidence** equals the **angle of reflection**.
 
• Hard surfaces are generally better reflectors of sound, whereas soft surfaces tend to absorb sound waves.
 
 
 
• **Stethoscope:**
 
 
• This is a medical instrument used by **doctors** to listen to sounds produced within the body, such as the **heartbeat** or **lung** sounds.
 
• It also works on the principle of **multiple reflection**, where the sound of the heartbeat travels through the **tube** via reflections to reach the doctor's ears.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Soundboards:** In large **concert halls** or **theaters**, **curved soundboards** are often placed behind the speaker or the stage so that sound, after reflection, spreads **uniformly** across the width of the hall.
 
• **Microphones vs. Megaphones:** It is important to distinguish that **microphones** are designed to **convert sound waves into electrical signals**, whereas **megaphones** are acoustic devices meant to **amplify and direct** existing sound waves through physical reflection.
 
• **Longitudinal Waves:** Sound travels through air as **longitudinal waves**, consisting of **compressions** and **rarefactions**. The ability to direct these waves through mechanical design is crucial in **acoustic engineering**.
 
• **Intensity and Amplitude:** The **loudness** of sound depends on its **amplitude**. By focusing the sound in one direction, the **amplitude** of the wave is maintained at a higher level over a greater distance than if the wave were allowed to expand **spherically**.
</ul

questions.question: A trader marked his goods 35% above its cost price. He then gave a discount of 15%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can use the successive percentage formula for net change: Net % = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100

Here, Markup (x) = +35% and Discount (y) = −15%.

Net Profit % = 35 − 15 + (35 × −15) ÷ 100

⇒ Profit % = 20 − 5.25 = 14.75%

**∴ The correct answer is 14.75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 35%

Discount Percentage = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP + Markup

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100

 
 
 
 
 Markup: +35% CP = 100 SP = 114.75 MP = 135 
 Discount: −15% 
 Profit: 14.75% 

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the goods be 100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 35% of 100 = 135

⇒ Discount = 15% of MP = (15 ÷ 100) × 135 = 20.25

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount = 135 − 20.25 = 114.75

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 114.75 − 100 = 14.75

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (14.75 ÷ 100) × 100 = 14.75%

**∴ The correct answer is 14.75%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price on the label of an article. Discount is always given on the Marked Price, while Profit/Loss is purely calculated on the Cost Price.

Successive Discount

When two discounts a% and b% are given successively, the equivalent single discount is [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Dishonest Dealer

A dealer who sells goods at CP but uses false weights. Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

**Calculation:**

12 + {6 × 27 ÷ 3 + 2} − (16 ÷ 8) × 5

⇒ 12 + {6 × 27 ÷ 3 + 2} − 2 × 5

⇒ 12 + {6 × 9 + 2} − (2) × 5

⇒ 12 + {54 + 2} − 10

⇒ 12 + 56 − 10

⇒ 68 − 10 = 58

It specifies the order of operations: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Order of Brackets

Always simplify the innermost brackets first, following the order: parenthesis ( ), then curly braces { }, and finally square brackets [ ].

Division and Multiplication share the same priority level and are solved from left to right. Similarly, Addition and Subtraction share the same priority and are also solved from left to right.

questions.question: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2022, seeks to amend the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950, with respect to its application to which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Fourth Amendment) Bill, 2022**, was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** on **December 9, 2022**, by the **Union Minister of Tribal Affairs**, **Shri Arjun Munda**.
 
• The primary objective of this bill is to amend the **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950**, specifically focusing on its application to the state of **Karnataka**.
 
• The bill seeks to include the **'Betta-Kuruba'** community as a synonym for the **'Kadu Kuruba'** community at **serial number 16** of the **Scheduled Tribes** list for **Karnataka**.
 
• This change was proposed because the **Betta-Kuruba** community had been facing difficulties in obtaining **Scheduled Tribe certificates** due to the absence of their specific name in the existing list, despite being ethnically identical to the **Kadu Kuruba**.
 
• The inclusion follows the formal recommendation of the **Government of Karnataka** and subsequent clearance by the **Registrar General of India (RGI)** and the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Framework for Scheduled Tribes**:
 
 
• Under **Article 342** of the **Constitution of India**, the **President**, after consultation with the **Governor** of a state, notifies the list of **Scheduled Tribes**.
 
• Once the initial list is notified via the **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950**, any subsequent inclusion, exclusion, or modification can only be done through an **Act of Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Inclusion**:
 
 
• Members of the **Betta-Kuruba** community will now be eligible for benefits under various government schemes, such as **Post-Matric Scholarships**, **National Overseas Scholarships**, and **Top Class Education** for **ST** students.
 
• It also ensures **political representation** in **Reserved Constituencies** and **reservation** in government jobs under **Article 16(4)** of the **Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Process of Amendment**:
 
 
• The process begins with a proposal from the **State Government**, which is then sent to the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs**.
 
• The **Registrar General of India (RGI)** reviews the ethnographical details. If approved, it is sent to the **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST)** for final consultation before being placed before the **Union Cabinet** and then **Parliament**.
 
 
 
• **Related 2022 Amendments**:
 
 
• Apart from **Karnataka**, the **Government of India** introduced similar bills in **2022** for states like **Tamil Nadu** (to include **Narikoravan** and **Kurivikkaran**), **Himachal Pradesh** (for **Hattee** community), and **Uttar Pradesh** (for **Gond** community in certain districts).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Betta-Kuruba** community traditionally resides in the hilly regions of **Kodagu**, **Mysuru**, and **Chamarajanagar** districts in **Karnataka**.
 
• They are traditionally known for their skills in **basket weaving** and **honey collection**.
 
• The term **'Betta'** means **Hill** and **'Kuruba'** refers to **Shepherd**, although this specific community is primarily forest-dwelling rather than pastoral.
 
• The **Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2022** reflects the government's commitment to **'Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas'** by providing social justice to marginalized communities.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is a major application of 3D bioprinting demonstrated at MSU Vadodara in 2025?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **2025**, **Maharaja Sayajirao University (MSU) Vadodara** showcased major advancements in **3D bioprinting**, specifically focusing on its transformative role in **regenerative medicine and tissue engineering**.
 
• The demonstration highlighted the ability to create **complex biological structures** by utilizing **living cells** and specialized **bio-inks**, which are deposited **layer-by-layer** to form functional tissues.
 
• This technology at **MSU Vadodara** aims to address critical healthcare challenges by developing **lab-grown tissues** such as **skin grafts**, **bone scaffolds**, and **vascular networks**.
 
• The application in **regenerative medicine** focuses on the **repair** and **replacement** of damaged organs or tissues, potentially eliminating the need for traditional **organ donors** in the future.
 
• The **2025** demonstration emphasized **precision medicine**, where **3D bioprinting** is used to create patient-specific models for **surgical planning** and **drug efficacy testing**.

__
 
• **3D Bioprinting**: This is an **additive manufacturing** process that uses **biological materials** to fabricate structures that imitate the characteristics of **natural tissues**. It differs from standard 3D printing by using **living cells** instead of plastic or metal.
 
• **Bio-inks**: These are the "inks" used in bioprinters, typically composed of **hydrogels**, **growth factors**, and **nutrients** that sustain **cell viability** and promote **proliferation** during and after the printing process.
 
• **Tissue Engineering**: This is a scientific field that combines **engineering** and **life sciences** to develop **biological substitutes**. It often uses a **scaffold** to provide a **three-dimensional** framework for cells to attach and grow.
 
• **Regenerative Medicine**: This branch of medicine seeks to **regenerate** human cells, tissues, or organs to restore **normal function**. It includes **stem cell therapy** and **bio-fabrication** as core components.
 
• **Future Applications**: Beyond tissue repair, **3D bioprinting** is expected to revolutionize **pharmaceutical research** by allowing scientists to test new **drugs** on **printed human tissues**, significantly reducing the necessity for **animal testing** and improving the accuracy of **clinical trials**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Precision and Customization**: One of the primary advantages of **3D bioprinting** is its ability to produce **anatomically accurate** structures tailored to a specific **patient's anatomy** using **MRI** or **CT scan** data.
 
• **Biocompatibility**: The materials used at institutions like **MSU Vadodara** are selected for their **biocompatibility**, ensuring that the printed tissues do not trigger an **immune rejection** when integrated with natural biological systems.
 
• **Economic Impact**: By localizing the production of **bio-printed tissues** and **scaffolds** in **India**, the technology helps in making **advanced healthcare** more **affordable** and accessible.
</ul

questions.question: The Reserve Bank of India revised Priority Sector Lending (PSL) guidelines for Small Finance Banks from FY 2025–26, reducing the PSL target to what percentage of ANBC (adjusted net bank credit) or Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposures (CEOBE)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**60%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in a notification issued in **April 2024**, announced a significant revision to the **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)** targets for **Small Finance Banks (SFBs)** to bring them on par with universal banks.
 
• As per the revised guidelines, the overall **PSL target** for **Small Finance Banks**, which was previously mandated at **75%**, will be reduced in a phased manner. For the financial year **2025–26** (specifically by **March 31, 2026**), the target has been set at **60%** of **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** or **Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE)**, whichever is higher.
 
• The primary objective of this revision is to provide a **level playing field** for **SFBs** and to harmonize their regulatory requirements with those of **Universal Banks**, which currently have a **40%** PSL target.
 
• Before this revision, **Small Finance Banks** were required to maintain a much higher threshold of **75%** to ensure that credit reached the **unserved and underserved sections** of the population, including small farmers and micro-units.
 
• The **RBI** has implemented a **glide path** for this transition: the target remains **75%** until **March 31, 2025**; it reduces to **60%** by **March 31, 2026**; and finally reaches **40%** by **March 31, 2027**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL):** It is a **regulatory framework** established by the **RBI** that mandates banks to allocate a specific portion of their **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** to certain sectors that are considered vital for the **inclusive development** of the country. These sectors include **Agriculture**, **Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)**, **Export Credit**, **Education**, **Housing**, **Social Infrastructure**, and **Renewable Energy**.
 
• **Small Finance Banks (SFBs):** These are a specific category of banks established to provide **financial inclusion** to sections of the economy not being served by other banks. They are registered as **public limited companies** under the **Companies Act, 2013** and are governed by the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**. Notable examples include **AU Small Finance Bank**, **Equitas Small Finance Bank**, and **Jana Small Finance Bank**.
 
• **ANBC and CEOBE:** **Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC)** represents the total credit provided by a bank after making specific adjustments for bills rediscounted and other prescribed exemptions. **Credit Equivalent of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE)** refers to the potential credit risk from non-fund-based limits like **letters of credit** or **bank guarantees**.
 
• **Regulatory Scope:** While the overall target is being reduced, **SFBs** are still required to focus on their core mission of serving **Small and Marginal Farmers** and **Weaker Sections**. The **RBI** maintains specific sub-targets within the PSL framework to ensure these vulnerable groups continue to receive adequate credit flow.

• **Eligibility for SFBs:** To be eligible for a license, the **minimum paid-up voting equity capital** for **SFBs** was initially **Rs. 100 crore**, which has been increased to **Rs. 200 crore** in recent guidelines, except for those transitioned from **Urban Co-operative Banks**.
 
• **The Glide Path Schedule:**
 
 
• **75%**: Applicable up to the end of **FY 2024-25**.
 
• **60%**: Target for the end of **FY 2025-26**.
 
• **40%**: Final target to be achieved by the end of **FY 2026-27**.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Revision:** This move is expected to improve the **profitability** and **operational flexibility** of **Small Finance Banks**, as they can now diversify their loan portfolios toward higher-yielding non-priority sectors as they grow in size and scale.
 
• **Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks (UCBs):** It is important to note that **UCBs** are also on a similar glide path to reach a **75%** PSL target by **March 31, 2026**, showing the **RBI's** efforts to balance different banking tiers according to their specific mandates and risks.
